branch_x.description: Automate drift monitoring with a dedicated tool

author.name: Model Monica
author.role: Specializes in designing, optimizing, and training machine learning models. Conducts data exploration and iterates on models to maximize predictive performance. Collaborates on model deployment, versioning, and performance monitoring.

challenge.name: The Warehouse Flood
challenge.description: A forecast job failed silently for three days, leaving stores ordering blind, and the team never knew until the warehouse was flooded with unsold promotion stock. #reliability_ruth# argues that the performance monitoring must be automated and governed to catch such failures instantly, while #efficiency_emilia# is willing to accept a manual monthly audit of the logs to save on tooling costs.

output.content: I asked for the production drift monitoring to be automated with a dedicated tool because manual checks will not catch a silent failure before the warehouse floods with unsold stock. If the dedicated tool is too expensive for the current budget, I would accept an in-house script instead. I am willing to give up the polished dashboard and automated alerting to keep the project moving, provided the script can flag when the forecast distribution shifts beyond our tolerance thresholds. My priority is catching drift early enough to prevent the next three day blind ordering incident, and I will trade the convenience of a commercial platform for a working solution if that is what the budget allows.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to give up the polished dashboard and automated alerting features of a commercial tool to accept a cheaper in-house script, prioritizing a working solution over convenience.
